review.reviewBody: Coming into New Life, I was 18 years old. From the moment I stepped into the house, I knew that this place was different. The community I gained from this house is something that has become so special to me. I have been pushed to become a person I am truly proud to be.

The house has given me a brotherhood and a community I can rely on. The house has given me the tools to work on myself and to grow spiritually, mentally, and physically. I'll forever be grateful for the people that have played a part in me getting sober at New Life.

I have had such a good experience here at New Life! The staff are great. The community is the #1 best thing about the house. Even the graduates find ways to stay involved. New Life has changed the direction of my life. I have meaningful relationships now. My relationship with my parents is finally on the upswing.

We were very lucky to have found this place for our son. They guided us from the beginning. The support from the staff and the other parents have been incredible. He graduated after 14 months. It has been a blessing.

New Life house completely changed my life. I was strung out on drugs and alcohol. The house helped me find my way to a better life. I found a purpose for living and gave me a relationship with my family once again. I can't explain how grateful I am for this program and the process!

itemOffered.name: Core Residential Program at New Life House
itemOffered.description: Our core residential program combines multiple treatment approaches in one supportive setting. Program includes morning meditation, shared breakfast with fellow residents, daily chores and structured morning activities, substance use and mental health treatment for residents in early recovery (in partnership with Clear Behavioral Health), life-skills programming including financial management, time management, and communication skills, attendance at outside recovery community events and meetings, participation in 12-step meetings, fun group activities and community-building events, scheduled free time and recreation, consistent peer engagement and support, and vocational phase work attendance.

itemOffered.name: Substance Use Treatment Program
itemOffered.description: Our Substance Use Treatment Program through our sister program, Clear Behavioral Health, offers personalized therapy, recovery support, and structure so you can regain control of your life and move forward with confidence. The program provides a comprehensive approach designed to help you manage and overcome addiction, personalized care through one-on-one therapy, group therapy, and medication management when needed, weekly individual sessions to explore your triggers, challenges, and goals, daily peer group therapy where clients learn from one another and build accountability, and holistic therapy through yoga, meditation, and music therapy to reconnect you with your body.

itemOffered.name: Outpatient Drug Treatment Program
itemOffered.description: Our Outpatient Drug Treatment Programs provide structured, evidence-based care for individuals seeking recovery while continuing work, school, or family responsibilities. Through our partnership with Clear Behavioral Health, we offer personalized treatment that supports long-term sobriety and emotional well-being. Services include flexible outpatient care focused on drug addiction recovery, individualized treatment plans including therapy, group counseling, and medication support when appropriate, weekly one-on-one therapy to address triggers and recovery goals, regular peer group sessions to build accountability and community, and holistic therapies such as meditation, yoga, and wellness activities.

itemOffered.name: Family Therapy Program
itemOffered.description: Our Family Therapy Program strengthens family relationships and creates a healthier support system for you during recovery. The program involves loved ones in the recovery journey so they can better understand addiction and your healing process, offers weekly family therapy to rebuild trust, improve communication, and resolve conflicts, provides biweekly group family therapy to connect with other families, build community, and trust within the group, helps families create a supportive, stable environment for long-term recovery, and empowers everyone involved to move forward together.

itemOffered.name: Educational Program
itemOffered.description: Our Educational Program helps you achieve your academic goals while developing life skills that support long-term independence. The program includes prioritized focus on education, personal development, and career planning, weekly learning activities including classes, workshops, vocational training, and life skills sessions, support for GED/college coursework, certifications, and academic pathways, and training in time management, organization, communication, and financial literacy.

itemOffered.name: Alumni Program
itemOffered.description: Our Alumni Program keeps you connected, supported, and motivated through a network of peers who understand your recovery journey. The program provides a strong peer community that stays connected long after clients graduate, weekly alumni meetings and events that promote accountability and support, yearly meet-ups with the extended alumni community and families, celebration of alumni milestones with sober birthdays and graduation parties, mentorship opportunities between alumni and newer clients, and a built-in support network to help you stay grounded and maintain your progress.

mainEntity.name: How long do clients typically stay in sober living?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most clients stay between 3–12 months, depending on their goals, progress, and the level of support needed. Some choose a shorter stay to reinforce early recovery skills, while others benefit from a longer, structured environment as they transition back into everyday life. At New Life House, your stay is tailored to what will best support your long term success.

mainEntity.name: What’s the difference between sober living and rehab?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rehab focuses on detox and intensive treatment, usually in a clinical or inpatient setting. Sober living, on the other hand, gives you a safe, substance-free home where you can apply what you learned in treatment to real life. It’s about building routines, practicing responsibility, strengthening coping skills, and gaining independence, with support from a sober community.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to complete treatment before entering a sober living home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most clients enter sober living after completing detox or primary treatment, but requirements vary based on your situation and clinical recommendations. If you’re unsure, our team can guide you toward the level of care that fits your needs and ensures a safe, stable transition through our partner organization, Clear Behavioral Health.

mainEntity.name: Can clients work or go to school while living in sober living?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it’s often encouraged. Sober living provides structure and accountability so you can return to work, school, or volunteer activities while still having a strong recovery foundation. You’ll have house expectations and curfews, but plenty of room to build a healthy, independent routine.

mainEntity.name: What is the environment like inside the house?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can expect a supportive, community oriented atmosphere where everyone is working toward the same goal: long-term sobriety. There’s structure, daily routines, peer accountability, and a sense of belonging. Clients cook, attend meetings, participate in house activities, and support each other through challenges and wins.

mainEntity.name: What kind of support does the staff provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: You’ll benefit from a team of experienced health experts, mentors, and counselors who offer guidance, weekly check ins, life skills support, and recovery focused programming. The goal is to help you stay grounded, motivated, and connected while you build the confidence to thrive on your own.

mainEntity.name: Is sober living suitable for young adults?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. Many sober living programs, including New Life House, are specifically designed for teens and young adults ages 18 and up, and offer age-appropriate support, structure, and community. Clients benefit from being surrounded by peers who understand what they’re going through and who are equally committed to recovery.

Yes. Family involvement can be a powerful part of recovery, and New Life House encourages ongoing communication, family therapy, and educational resources. The goal is to help loved ones understand the recovery process and support you in healthy, constructive ways.

How sober living for men works

The process of joining one of our sober living homes is simple, and thoughtfully designed to help you feel comfortable and prepared. Here’s how it works:

1. Reach out

Contact our admissions team at 424-722-4262 to discuss your needs and determine if our sober living environment is a suitable fit.

2. Assessment

We’ll conduct a brief assessment to understand your background, recovery goals, and readiness for structured support.

3. Move-in & orientation

Once you’re ready, you’ll join the house, meet your peers, and get familiar with the routines and expectations.

4. Daily structure

You’ll follow a schedule that includes meetings, therapy (when applicable), curfews, and regular drug testing.

5. Build community

As you settle in, you’ll participate in group activities, house responsibilities, and peer support.

6. Recovery integration

Over time, you’ll develop healthy routines, build life and coping skills, pursue education or employment, and regain independence with a strong support network in place.

Why choose New Life House?

New Life House in Los Angeles is one of the most trusted and structured sober living homes for men in California, built on decades of experience and a proven approach for long term recovery.

These benefits come together to create an environment where you can stay accountable, build confidence, and grow into your healthiest, most independent self.
